subjects.displayTitle: Developing capacity: preparation, receptivity, and the gift of grace
subjects.introduction: The oil, the wick, the glass and the bowl can all be gathered, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, and still a lamp is not alight until a hand brings the flame; yet it is the readiness of the lamp that draws the hand. Capacity is like that. It is not a fixed allotment but something a person enlarges, by study that polishes the mirror, by prayer that widens the vessel, by sincerity, striving and service, by the ploughed field that calls down the rain. And it is never a claim on God: beside the grace that answers seeking there is a bounty given freely, and even the intention to grow is already a gift. The teaching is tender about limits too, warning that a person able to carry fifty kilos will fall under a hundred. Mark’s sower, whose seed meets stony ground, thorns and good earth, asks what helps a promising response take root. The path continues into education and the development of capacity, into the differences in human capacity a wise teacher honours, and into every human being’s power to recognise the truth.
subjects.arc: Open with growing receptivity and freely given grace; explore latent powers, cultivation, and wise teaching; consider obstacles and differing responses; then turn capacity toward service, gratitude, and prayer.

order.why: Hear the reported affirmation that the world has capacity and needs teachers.
Open with prayer as an enlargement of the vessel of capacity.
shortened: Therefore, during thy supplications to GOD and thy reciting "Thy Name is my healing" - consider how thine heart is cheered up, thy soul delighteth by the spirit of the Love of GOD, and thy mind becomes attracted to the Kingdom of GOD! By these attractions, one's ability and capacity increase. When the vessel is widened the water increaseth, and when the thirst grows the bounty of the cloud becomes agreeable to the taste of man. This is the mystery of supplication and the wisdom of stating one's wants (praying).

order.why: Place freely given bounty beside the language of preparation.
shortened: O thou flame of the fire of the love of God!

There is a grace and mercy in existence which can be requested, and this is mostly according to capacity and seeking. And there is a bounty and generosity which depends neither on capacity and receptivity nor on asking and requesting, but is purely a gift.

order.why: Consider study as polishing and the seed as latent possibility.
Keep moderation and common sense beside the call to grow.
Read the reported recognition of intention itself as capacity.
Introduce the sower and receptive soil.
shortened: Therefore, we must ever strive for capacity and seek readiness. As long as we lack susceptibility, the beauties and bounties of God cannot penetrate. Christ spoke a parable in which He said His words were like the seeds of the sower; some fall upon stony ground, some upon sterile soil, some are choked by thorns and thistles, but some fall upon the ready, receptive and fertile ground of human hearts.

order.why: Distinguish knowledge gained through effort from the grace that awakens faith.
Read the statement of original purity and formative influences.
Keep the reported affirmation of newborn goodness in its own terms.
Explore the reported distinction between innate and acquired perfections.
shortened: All things have qualities which are created with them -which are innate in them. The brilliance of the stars, the beauty of the trees, the brightness of the ocean, the fragrance of the flowers, -all these qualities are innate in the objects to which they pertain. Man, also, has innate qualities; but there is in addition a perfection, not innate, which may be acquired by him.

order.why: Explains the development of innate capacity through education and personal effort.
Read the reported need to acquire capacities through effort.
shortened: To birds and beasts God has given all those things which it is necessary for them to have. But he has created man without giving him these things; he must acquire them by his own efforts.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of degrees of life as its explanatory framework.
Consider embryonic capacities as an image of preparation for another world.
shortened: He likened it to the child in the matrix. It has eyes, ears, hands, feet, etc, but these powers are not in activity, not to be used in the matrix world. The whole purpose of the matrix life is the coming forth into this world, so the whole purpose of this life is the coming forth into the world of reality, when all these forces will then be in their proper sphere for activity. They belong to that world.

order.why: Read the reported question and answer about potentiality before embodiment.
Consider the reported contrast between seeing an egg and discerning its possibilities.
shortened: A wise man when looking at an egg, sees in it the whole form of a bird; he sees the beak, the claws, the plumage, the wings and the eyes, as well as the song and melody of the bird; but a child or an unwise man sees nothing but the egg, even unable to go any further than the outward shell and appearance.

order.why: Read the reported universal gift as latent before becoming manifest.
Consider the human capacity to carry the trust.
shortened: It is man who can carry this trust. Consider what a gift and bestowal this is, that it has preceded all created things, and the mightiest forces of the world cannot resist it.

order.why: Read the invitation to undertake that trust.
shortened: Withhold not thyself from bearing the trust which neither the heavens nor the earth could bear, save whom thy Lord willeth.

order.why: Keep the cup and ocean image as a reflection on measure and limits.
Consider different effects of one cause according to receptivity.
shortened: For instance, observe how one effect proceeds from a cause. This cause is single, yet in each soul it is transformed according to that soul's capacity and its effects become manifest. In each station it appears with a different manifestation.

order.why: Read the concise statement of reception according to capacity.
shortened: In this first age of the Chosen Beauty, the divine bounty exists in its utmost power and encompasses all beings. Yet each created thing receives and benefits according to its capacity.

order.why: Keep the reported difference of degree within a shared gift.
Read the reported account of preparation and bounty without collapsing its distinction.
Preserve the companion report of unusual preparation separately.
shortened: Some attain to the highest station because they are so well prepared that they can enter the highest station without earthly preparation. When we see a child wise beyond his years, it is a sign of this preparation, so we cannot question the justice of this.

order.why: Consider the possibility of progress without knowledge of a foreign language.
shortened: The essential thing is capacity. One who has capacity and is confirmed will make progress, whether they know a foreign language or not. One who lacks capacity, even if they know multiple foreign languages, will yield no fruit from their existence.

order.why: Keep the reported value of language knowledge as a distinct emphasis.
shortened: It feeleth the warmth of the sun, but perceiveth not the effulgence of its rays. Yet there were souls who were gladdened by the glad-tidings of God and attracted by the fragrances of God. Had they known Persian and understood Arabic, they would have been greatly moved.

order.why: Read the reported connection of capacity with striving and sincerity.
shortened: Capacity is in accordance with striving and sincerity.

order.why: Consider patient searching for successive treasures in one’s environment.
Explore polishing through effort alongside the appointed season of fruit.
Read daily enlargement and refinement of the mirror.
Keep the concise connection between refinement and reflected light.
Consider open bounty and the differing clarity of mirrors.
shortened: Praise be to God the divine bounty favors all of you, the doors of gifts are open before the faces of you all, and the radiance of the Sun of Truth is shining upon you all. Capacity, worth (or merit) and ability, are necessary, for the clearer and purer the mirror is, the lights of the Sun are more manifest thereon.

order.why: Read turning toward the source of light as increasing capacity.
shortened: The lights of earth are all acceptable, but the center of effulgence is the sun, and we must direct our gaze to the sun. God is the Supreme Center. The more we turn toward this Center of Light, the greater will be our capacity.

order.why: Join effort and preparation with supplication for capacity.
shortened: Although the bestowal is great and the grace is glorious, yet capacity and readiness are requisite. Without capacity and readiness the divine bounty will not become manifest and evident. No matter how much the cloud may rain, the sun may shine and the breezes blow, the soil that is sterile will give no growth.
Therefore, we must develop capacity in order that the signs of the mercy of the Lord may be revealed in us.
Therefore, we must endeavor always, cry, supplicate and invoke the Kingdom of God to grant us full capacity in order that the bestowals of God may become revealed and manifest in us.

order.why: Consider cultivating the ground for rain’s effects.
Read the reported lamp whose gathered materials await ignition.
shortened: Look at this lamp and consider its real condition. When every material of it, as the bowl, the glass, the oil, and the wick have been gathered together, they require a hand to put a flame to it and to light it up, so forming a real lamp. What is the power that attracts the hand to light it? It is the capacity of the lamp itself. When the soil is plowed and the seed scattered in it, a capacity is created which attracts the shower of the mercy of God.

order.why: Keep the contrast between a prepared lamp and wet wood.
shortened: The lamp that is endowed with capacity will be instantly lit when brought close to fire while a wet log when cast amidst the flames will send forth nothing save smoke.

order.why: Read the images of near-shining oil and productive earth.
shortened: But the oil of the Blessed Tree would well-nigh shine forth even if no fire touched it - this is from capacity.
The good land bringeth forth its vegetation by permission of its Lord, while that which is bad bringeth forth naught but scanty growth.

order.why: Consider good soil through the benefit it yields to people.
shortened: Know that barren soil wasteth what is cast therein, while good earth bringeth forth what benefiteth its people.

order.why: Keep the source’s contrast between fruitful and unfruitful ground.
shortened: As for the good earth, the blessed soil - it brought forth its vegetation by the leave of its Lord. But that which is corrupt bringeth forth naught but that which is worthless.

order.why: Read the spring rain image as a question about reception.
Keep the reported salty-soil analogy in its own terms.
Read the reported counsel to sow in fertile ground.
Consider confirmation alongside the need for receptive soil.
shortened: O Ustad! Divine confirmation is thy companion and heavenly assistance thy strong support. Yet capacity is needed. Pure soil is required for the rain of mercy to bring forth flowers and sweet herbs, and a pure gem is needed to receive the bounty of the sun of the heavens. Otherwise, black earth can never become the repository of a radiant pearl.

order.why: Read the invitation to show capacity through response.
shortened: Show forth thy capacity and merit, for without capacity the Gift doth not become manifest.

order.why: Keep the brief insistence on sufficient capacity.
Consider the relation the source draws between capacity and assurance.
shortened: Capacity is essential; the more capacity thou findest, the more assurance shall be attained. The more a mirror is polished, the more will the rays of the sun be reflected therein.

order.why: Hear the reported call to prepare for further grace.
shortened: You thank God a hundred thousand times at every moment that you have become the recipient of such bounties. You must make yourselves ready so as to receive more and more of these heavenly Graces.

order.why: Read the reported hunger and maternal nourishment image.
Consider the reported difference between a larger and smaller vessel.
shortened: There are certain souls whose thirst is never allayed, while others are satisfied with one drop. The larger the vase the greater its capacity to hold water, but when the vase is small, there will be very little water in it.

order.why: Read thirst as an image of increasing reception.
Keep the reported thirst for life-giving water.
shortened: Only the thirsty crave the 'Salabil of the Euphrates' (Water of Life), but if one be not thirsty he cares not for this Life-giving water. Only the spirits attracted by the fragrances of GOD can enjoy the mention of GOD.

order.why: Read the reported cluster of thirst, hunger, fragrance, and soil images.
Consider recognizing the value of a gift through need and receptivity.
shortened: This is a supreme gift if one knows its value. Otherwise, to the foolish, guidance or misguidance are the same. One who is not thirsty cannot know the sweetness of pure water, and likewise what benefit can saline soil derive from spring clouds, or what portion can a withered tree receive from April showers?

order.why: Read the reported desire for divine life amid material concerns.
shortened: Jesus declares that there is spiritual capacity in some people, for all are not submerged in the sea of materialism. They seek the Divine Spirit; they turn to God; they long for the Kingdom.

order.why: Consider freedom from conditions that obstruct spiritual progress.
Keep illumination, desire, and capacity together in the reported statement.
Read the reported contrast between continuing desire and premature satisfaction.
shortened: Some souls, when they drink from the cup of recognition, cry out "Is there more?" Others, on the contrary, upon seeing a mirage consider themselves satisfied and display self-sufficiency, like the Children of Israel in the day of the appearance of Christ.

order.why: Consider the report of a visit that leaves the visitor unchanged.
Keep the reported contrast between different responses to the same presence.
shortened: Many came and attained the hallowed presence of Baha'u'llah, witnessed His heavenly ways, the warmth of His smile, His divine attraction and His infinite bounties, yet they would leave the same way that they came, unchanged. However, others, upon their very arrival, would gain a new life and be thoroughly transformed.

order.why: Preserve the companion observation about awakening and unchanged return.
shortened: Some come to this Land and are awakened and enkindled [with the love of God]. Others come and return in the same state as before.

order.why: Read the reported distinction between duration and the capacity to become enkindled.
shortened: Some people stay a short time, and then go and do great service. Other people are here a long time, and they learn nothing.
There is some wood that is very dry; it catches fire quickly and burns well. There is other wood that is so wet that it will not burn even though you should try for a whole day.

order.why: Consider the reported examples of receptivity rather than length of stay.
Keep the reported comparison of geographic distance and receptivity historically attributed.
Read nearness without transformation beside a personal gift of grace.
shortened: There are thousands of people in the Holy Land associated with us and yet they are deprived and have no hope in God. This is naught save a blessing from the Heavenly Father which hath enlightened that face (i. e., thy face) and made that heart (thy heart) divine.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast between Peter’s receptivity and outward rank.
shortened: Peter was only a catcher of fishes, yet his attainment was very great. Ananias, the High Priest, was much greater in the eyes of the world, yet he was deprived while Peter received the Bounty of God.

order.why: Read the warning that confidence in one’s advancement can conceal need.
shortened: Reflect upon God's vast grace and mercy - those who considered themselves the most advanced, ancient, ascetic and God-fearing remained heedless and veiled from the Cause and reason of creation, while you, through divine grace, attained recognition of God, exalted be His glory, on the Lord of Days and turned toward the highest horizon.

order.why: Keep the reported personal address concerning response to a call.
Read the reported recognition of capacity through an existing response.
Consider awakening itself as evidence of ability.
Read gratitude for hearing the call.
Consider encouragement of a particular person’s evident capacities.
Read the prayer for growth, clearer perception, and eternal life.
shortened: And I beseech God that Mr. Fukuta may progress day by day and that the women of Japan may rend asunder the veils of idle fancies and witness the lights of reality, seek eternal life and desire everlasting bounty.

order.why: Hear the encouragement toward daily progress and discerning vision.
Consider training as the response to undeveloped capacities.
Read the reported call to teach from the listener’s standpoint and by degrees.
Keep the reported need for varied ways of expression.
Read the reported attention to the time and the listeners.
Keep the Bab’s counsel about sharing wisdom with attention to receptivity.
shortened: Guard ye God's mystery within you, for God hath appointed for you a station upon the Path. Give not wisdom unto the foolish, for they have believed in God, the Most High, and His mystery weakly, upon the ocean of weakness.

order.why: Read the reported connection between moral formation and capacity for government.
Turn the consideration of capacity toward serving a parent.
shortened: Do not spare any effort in serving your father, for he was the cause of your guidance to the path of salvation and your receiving abundance from the spirit of life.

order.why: Read the hope that receptive people arise to reform the world.
shortened: It is hoped that God, exalted be His glory, through the steadfastness and orientation of His trusted ones and chosen ones, will raise up a people who will take heed and arise for the reformation of the world.

order.why: Join service and inner vision to gratitude and further prayer.
Consider the reported joy of fruitful service.
shortened: Praise be to God, you are sowing your seeds in fertile and most blessed soil, wherein they will grow and flourish and yield good fruit. The harvest will be boundless and everlasting. If you be not happy, who could be happy? You have entered the world in the day of Baha'u'llah. You have harkened to the summons of Baha'u'llah. You have turned to the kingdom of Baha'u'llah and are manifesting the favors of Baha'u'llah. Verily the light of the Most Great Guidance has become iridescent in your hearts, and in the wilderness of the world you are proving to be fruitful trees.

order.why: Keep the reported example of courage amid threatening power.
shortened: Consider then, in such an assembly, at a time when Nasiri'd-Din Shah was at the height of his bloodthirstiness and the Nayibu's-Saltanih at the peak of his recklessness, with attendants and executioners standing by with whips and swords - it is evident with what power and what spirit that noble person (may my soul be a sacrifice unto him) did speak. How pure in faith was this person!

order.why: Read the reported possibility of assistance through even a slight inclination.
Consider the reported effect of a single word upon a receptive soul.
shortened: If he has the capacity, a single divine word can enkindle him and his life is strengthened by a single word of God. But if he has not the capacity and one speaks to him always of spiritual things, it is of no effect.

order.why: Read the source’s account of qualities enabling rapid reception.
Consider valuing an opportunity so its effects become visible.
Keep the call to cherish and preserve a bounty.
Read the warning about losing a spiritual station.
Consider sharing what one has received with others.
Read insight as recognition amid obstructing veils.
Keep the concise connection between opened eyes and understanding intent.
shortened: Those whose eyes have been opened - these are they who recognize therein what their Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, intended thereby.

order.why: Read the effort to use sight and hearing for their stated purpose.
shortened: Strive thou that perchance thine eyes may be enabled to perceive that for which they were created, and likewise thine ears to hearken unto the Call that is raised.

order.why: Consider sight and hearing interpreted through recognition and acknowledgment.
Read the blessing on inward hearing and pure vision.
shortened: Blessed are they who have heard His call with the ear of the soul and beheld His horizon with the most pure vision.

order.why: Keep the source’s hearing and speech metaphors together.
shortened: The deaf ear surely heareth not the divine call, and the dumb tongue engageth not in divine praise. Praise be to God that the hearing was so acute that the attentive ear heard the divine Word.

order.why: Read the contrast between summoned perception and negligence.
Consider the sensory images as the source’s language of spiritual reception.
Keep the images of sight, smell, and hearing in their metaphorical setting.
shortened: If eyes are illumined, the lights are manifest, and if nostrils are open, the horizons are perfumed with holy fragrances. But if souls are blind and deaf, they are surely fruitless, for one with a cold cannot smell the fragrance of musk, and the blind one is veiled from beholding the subtle light.

order.why: Read Jacob’s discernment of fragrance as a figure for recognition.
Consider the reported garden whose beauties require receptive perception.
shortened: The divine kingdom is like a beautiful garden but if the people who enter into that garden be blind they cannot realize anything from the beauty of the flowers, and if they should be deaf they cannot hear the melodies of the nightingale of that garden, and if they have caught cold they cannot smell the fragrances of the flowers.
And so it is with the divine kingdom of God. Its stores are open - those who have capacity can get the benefit, and if they have not capacity they will get no benefit at all.

order.why: Read the reported approach to a garden as newly awakened experience.
Keep the reported account of spiritual perception and birth.
Consider attention as a condition of understanding another’s words.
Read the reported connection between perception and release from attachment.
Keep the sun and sight image as a spiritual analogy.
Distinguish describing a reality from experiencing it.
Read the source’s scriptural images of unseeing eyes and unhearing ears.
Keep the concise contrast concerning perception.
shortened: The seeing one beholdeth and witnesseth, while he who is gathered blind neither seeth nor perceiveth.

order.why: Read perception itself as illumined by grace.
Consider the contrast between turned and rusted mirrors.
Keep the reported stone and mirror analogy in its own terms.
Read the sequence of vision, nourishment, and fitness images.
Consider the stated prerequisites for reflecting love.
shortened: There is no grace greater in the world of existence than this love. It is the most mighty sign the most wondrous bounty to the world of humanity. But since its conditions and its prerequisites are mighty indeed, not all things can bear it nor do all creatures have the capacity of reflecting it. They are unable to do so.

order.why: Read the source’s account of prayer and capacity beside its other teachings on grace.
shortened: But you must become believing and assured, and the light of the love of God must radiate from you, for the prayer to have effect. If you pray for pure earth to become green and verdant, it will be answered, but if you pray for a rock to become a flower garden and meadow, it lacks the capacity. The acceptance of prayer depends upon capacity.

order.why: Keep the reported counteremphasis that acceptance depends upon divine favor.
shortened: Christ said that the Pharisee's praying was not accepted in the Kingdom of GOD, but the prayer of the poor man was accepted. It is therefore evident that acceptance depends upon the favor of GOD and is not according to capacity.

order.why: Read gratitude that disclaims a prior claim of worthiness.
Keep the concise acknowledgment of a gift.
Join progress with grace and assistance.
shortened: This dependeth upon divine grace and assistance. We counsel all the friends to that which is the cause of progress and the means of elevation.

order.why: Read the prayer for what will truly profit the recipient.
Keep the praise of a spiritual aspiration in its addressed setting.
shortened: Excellent is what thou hast desired for thyself, for this is a matter greater and more glorious in the sight of God thy Lord than any other matter, if thou be of those who perceive, and nothing that hath been created between the heavens and earth can compare with it.

order.why: Read the hope of attaining a great bounty.
Hear the image of approaching breezes of grace.
Preserve the brief image of earth receiving a share from the cup.
Consider fragrance and radiance guiding those who long for God.
Read the invitation to fountain, garden, and sea.
shortened: I hope that you will have a share of this Fountain; that you will inhale the perfume of the roses of this Garden; that you will swim in the water and partake of all the beautiful pearls which exist in the bottom of the Sea.

order.why: Keep the personal thanksgiving for recognition.
Read the named recipient’s remembrance and blessing.
shortened: O 'Inayatu'llah-i-'Attar, upon thee be the glory of the Unconstrained! Mention hath been made of thee, therefore the gaze of loving-kindness is turned toward thee and He hath blessed thee with the signs of the Most Exalted Pen.

order.why: Consider wisdom drawn from the treasury of utterance.
shortened: Blessed are they who have derived wisdom from the treasury of the utterance of the All-Merciful and who have attained unto the bounties of His days.

order.why: Read the hope for continuing recognition and bounty.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath attained unto this most exalted station and this most sublime and resplendent horizon, and woe unto the heedless. Through the grace and favor of the Beloved of all creation, may your honor be successful at all times in attaining the supreme gift and greatest bounty, which is the recognition of the Manifestation of God's commandments.

order.why: Keep the command described as favor from the source.
Consider attachment to the tree as a figure of receiving good.
Read the urgency of an opportunity within a passing life.
shortened: Blessed is the soul that today acquireth eternal stations and attaineth unto a matter whose mention floweth from the Supreme Pen, and if one attaineth not unto this station, he shall pass from this ephemeral world with utmost regret.

order.why: Keep the source’s strong expression of the value of its Day.
Hear the brief call to strive against deprivation.
shortened: Strive that thou remain not deprived and portionless of that which is with God.

order.why: Read strength and penetrating vision amid doubts.
Consider the autumn-leaf image of an unsettled response to trials.
shortened: Those souls who are deprived of the Merciful One's presence by the blowing winds of trials are like autumn leaves that fall from the tree at a single gust.

order.why: Read the warning against allowing another’s words to obscure recognition.
Consider the contrast between desire and guidance.
Read the source’s account of veils being torn aside.
Keep the contrast between wandering and receiving bounty in its addressed setting.
shortened: Yet many souls in the Days of God have remained deprived of the wine of the All-Merciful's mercy and the Heavenly Fountain of Divine utterance, and wander bewildered in the wilderness of self and passion, while others have attained unto His infinite bounties.

order.why: Read the source’s lament over unresponsiveness amid abundant grace.
shortened: Not every soul hath been or shall be worthy of the Kawthar of inner meanings and receptive to the choice wine of divine love, as is evident when, despite the dawning of the Sun of bounty from the horizon of the world, most remain veiled from it.

order.why: Consider the presence of bounty alongside its unrecognized availability.
shortened: The choice wine existeth, the Cause is manifest, and the bounty is evident, yet the people are deprived save whom God willeth, the Mighty, the Beloved.

order.why: Keep the brief statement concerning receptivity to the fountain.
shortened: Not every soul was or is worthy of this most pure Kawthar.

order.why: Read the wilderness image for deprivation of bounty.
shortened: Blessed is he who takes his portion from the Most Great Ocean and arises amidst the peoples with this Name which God has made the Sovereign of names in the kingdom of creation, and through which He has attracted the hearts of those who believe in His unity. Verily, those who are deprived of this bounty wander lost in the wilderness of ignorance.

order.why: Consider the source’s account of utterance restrained by lack of receptivity.
Keep the conditional account of obstruction within its historical address.
shortened: I swear by My beauty that were it not for the prevention of preventers, the oppression of oppressors, and the obstruction of deniers from among the people of the Bayan, We would have commanded all things to seek knowledge of what was and what will be, and would have honored them all with this mighty robe and this most glorious garment.

order.why: Read the source’s contrast between stony response and tears of recognition.
Keep the unformed-embryo and cut-wing images in their admonitory setting.
Read the sharply contrasting responses to the same Day as the source portrays them.
Keep the severe animal and fragrance imagery attributed to the source.
Read the covenant passage’s polemical imagery within its particular address.
shortened: For not every fattened cow can prance in the field of the Covenant, and not every broken-winged crow can soar in the heights of recognition. Birds of the holy gardens are needed to warble of the truths of the ancient covenant, and lions of the valley of glory are needed to raise an uproar in the expanses of steadfastness.

order.why: Keep the reported critique of material preoccupation in its own language.
Read the rock, withered branch, and tree imagery as a warning about unresponsiveness.
Consider the reported lament for unrealized spiritual life.
shortened: Any soul who is deprived of the Graces of the worlds of God will remain portionless. He is like unto a child who does not possess objectively the irradiations of the intellect. He is like unto a piece of stone which is devoid of any human sensibilities. How pitiful is the condition of that soul who is uninformed with the Graces of the worlds of God.

order.why: Keep the reported magnet analogy beside other accounts of attraction.
shortened: Iron attracts iron, and as you approach the kingdom of God, you will be attracted by the things of the kingdom. Worldly people are not of the kind to be affected by the magnet.

order.why: Read the reported distinction between symbolic and clear experiences without endorsing private claims.
Keep the reported Cairo and rainfall example as the account’s claim, not an editorial scientific explanation.
Turn toward the reported hope for clearer perception and fuller attention.
shortened: I hope that you may become assisted and confirmed in the good pleasure of the Lord...
May your spiritual perception become keener, your attention to God more complete and your spirituality an example for others.

order.why: Read the prayer for discernment and steadfast remembrance.
shortened: Help them, then, O God, to reach forth, through the power of Thy sovereign might, towards such a station that they can readily distinguish every foul smell from the fragrance of the raiment of Him Who is the Bearer of Thy most lofty and exalted name, that they may turn with all their affections toward Thee, and may enjoy such intimate communion with Thee that if all that is in heaven and on earth were given them they would regard it as unworthy of their notice, and would refuse to cease from remembering Thee and from extolling Thy virtues.

order.why: Consider the prayer to clear the sight of created beings.
shortened: Clear away, then, the sight of Thy creatures, O my God, that they may recognize Him Who showeth forth the Godhead as One Who is sanctified from all that pertaineth unto them, and Who, wholly for Thy sake, is summoning them to the horizon of Thy unity, at a time when every moment of His life is beset with peril.

order.why: Read the prayer’s hope that people use their given faculties.
shortened: I testify that if Thy servants were to turn towards Thee with the eyes Thou didst create in them and with the ears wherewith Thou didst endow them, they would all be carried away by a single word sent down from the right hand of the throne of Thy majesty.

order.why: Keep thanksgiving for freedom from obstructing fancies.
shortened: O my God! These are servants whom the veils of idle fancies have not withheld from knowing Thee and drawing nigh unto the Dawning-Place of Thine inspiration, and whom the veils of mankind have not prevented from beholding the lights of Thy beauty.

order.why: Read weakness reaching toward strength and nearness.
shortened: O my Lord! Thou seest the weak one clinging to the cord of Thy strength, and him who was far off drawing nigh unto the horizon of Thy nearness. I beseech Thee not to disappoint him of that which lieth with Thee.

order.why: Consider the prayer for preservation and divine generosity.
Read the plea for guidance beyond idle fancies.
shortened: O Lord! Take the hand of this poor one with the hand of Thy bounty, then deliver him from the darkness of idle fancies through Thy power and might. Write down for him that which will draw him nigh unto Thee in every world of Thy worlds.

order.why: Join readiness with love, guidance, and responsive action.
Close with capacity expressed as steadfast love that gives light.
shortened: O God, grant capacity and bestow capability so that we may achieve supreme steadfastness and pass beyond this world and its people, and kindle the fire of Your love and like a candle burn and melt away and give light.

questions: How do the images of soil, mirrors, lamps, and vessels illuminate different aspects of developing capacity?
How can deliberate effort and the recognition of freely given grace strengthen rather than cancel one another?
What forms of study, prayer, service, or patient practice might enlarge receptivity in daily life?
How might a teacher recognize differing needs while honoring every person’s potential and avoiding excessive burdens?
What do the obstacles and fruitful responses in Mark’s parable suggest about the conditions of lasting growth?
Which neighboring subject on education, gradual progress, or universal spiritual capacity would help you explore a possibility in yourself or your community?

references.note: Read the sower’s seed meeting different conditions, and Jesus’ account of hearing, short-lived response, competing concerns, and fruitfulness. Compare these with the compilation’s images of prepared soil and enlarged receptivity. What practices and relationships might help a promising response take root and endure?

subjects.displayTitle: Calamities and war: warning, human responsibility, and the work of peace
subjects.introduction: A mother rending her garment, a merchant ruined in an hour and then marched to the front, children left without a father: Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá count the cost of war in households before they speak of nations. Their warnings are severe, yet never fatalism. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls the world a sick body whose physicians quarrel over the diagnosis, names prejudice, greed for profit and the lust of conquest as the axes laid to the root of humanity, and says that the war was not an act of God but the harvest of accumulated human deeds. To hear such warnings well means asking who spoke, when, and with what authority, and remembering the Guardian’s caution against imagining comets and catastrophes nowhere promised. Luke records Jesus refusing to treat the victims of a fallen tower as worse sinners and turning the question back on his listeners; that same turn toward the hearer governs ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s appeals to education, healing and steadfast service. From here the way leads into the contrast of war and peace, the renewal that follows corruption, and the imagery of the apocalypse.
subjects.arc: Begin with the human costs of war and the practical fruits of peace; investigate destructive causes and warnings in context; distinguish source kinds and limits of prediction; then turn toward healing, renewal, and sustained service.

order.why: Consider a warning that calls for action to avert harm.
Open with the grief of children, parents, and bereaved families.
shortened: How many the cities wherein the exalted were reduced to naught! How numerous the children that were orphaned and the women that were bereaved! How many a time hath a mother cried out with a bitter cry, rending her garment from the raging of her heart and the flood of her tears! How oft hath a father grieved for a mother's loss, weeping from morning till night!

order.why: Place the concrete benefits of prolonged peace beside those losses.
Introduce education and good character as a response to darkness.
shortened: Trust in God and think about educating humanity, sacrifice yourselves, and through good character and illumined nature make this dark world luminous. For the world is very dark and human society is like hell and the inferno.

order.why: Read the explicit rejection of unfounded claims about earthquakes after the war.
Read the diagnosis of a defective order and unused powers of discernment.
shortened: This humble servant is filled with wonder, inasmuch as all men are endowed with the capacity to see and hear, yet we find them deprived of the privilege of using these faculties.  This servant hath been prompted to pen these lines by virtue of the tender love he cherisheth for thee. The winds of despair are, alas, blowing from every direction, and strife that divideth and afflicteth the human race is daily increasing.  The signs of impending convulsions and chaos can now be discerned, inasmuch as the prevailing order appeareth to be lamentably defective.

order.why: Identify prejudices, profit, conquest, and hatred as implements of destruction.
Keep the reported attribution of war to accumulated human deeds.
Examine armaments and the self-interest hidden behind public claims.
shortened: The apparatus of conflict will, as preparations go on at their present rate, reach the point where war will become something intolerable to mankind.

What an extraordinary situation now obtains, when no one, hearing a claim advanced, asks himself what the speaker's real motive might be, and what selfish purpose he might not have hidden behind the mask of words. You find, for example, that an individual seeking to further his own petty and personal concerns, will block the advancement of an entire people. To turn his own water mill, he will let the farms and fields of all the others parch and wither. To maintain his own leadership, he will everlastingly direct the masses toward that prejudice and fanaticism which subvert the very base of civilization.

order.why: Read the reported interaction of economic, religious, racial, and political antagonisms.
shortened: The keen competition which is carried on by the captains of industry and finance; the discontent and social unrest of the laboring classes; the bigotry and extreme fanaticism of religionists; the heat and bitterness with which fantastic controversies are upheld between sectarians; the spirit of superiority with which some nations look upon others; the lust of conquest and the desire for the extension of territory; the social and political rivalries between nations and governments, and the hatred and enmity existing between the different races:--all these antagonistic forces clashing against each other, apparently aggravate the situation and make "confusion worse confounded."

order.why: Consider the reported need to join material development with spiritual qualities.
Read the reported formation of a new body politic amid changing practices.
shortened: In this radiant century neither the old customs nor the old sciences, crafts, laws and regulations have remained. The old political principles are undergoing change, and a new body politic is in process of formation.

order.why: Consider the call to remind people amid sedition.
shortened: Remind the people in these days wherein the fire of sedition hath been kindled and its darkness hath encompassed the servants.

order.why: Read the invitation to investigate the foundations of fellowship.
shortened: Therefore, it is our duty in this radiant century to investigate the essentials of divine religion, seek the realities underlying the oneness of the world of humanity and discover the source of fellowship and agreement which will unite mankind in the heavenly bond of love.

For if we remain fettered and restricted by human inventions and dogmas, day by day the world of mankind will be degraded, day by day warfare and strife will increase and satanic forces converge toward the destruction of the human race.

order.why: Keep the reported critique of invented means of destruction.
shortened: I want to tell you that most of the nations and the majority of the people are in perfect ignorance.

They are trying night and day to do something to destroy the foundation of man. There are among them political fights and wars. There are conflicts and disturbances. Every day they are inventing new instruments for the destruction of human life. There are among them also religious disputes and conflicts and disputes of patriotism. You hardly find two men between whom there is real harmony and sympathy.

order.why: Consider material progress diverted toward war.
Read the reported anticipation of increasingly destructive warfare from the air.
Keep the reported description of a destructive invention in its historical setting.
Read the reported connection between ongoing bloodshed and preparation for wider war.
Consider the reported appeal to extinguish the powder magazine before ignition.
Read the source’s recollection of warnings delivered in Western gatherings.
Keep the warning of an inflammable Europe within the source’s argument.
shortened: He completed the proof for all creation and in great gatherings and grand churches openly spread the blessed teachings and clearly explained to all that if these teachings are not promoted and followed, a devastating calamity lies ahead and all European countries are like an ammunition depot full of inflammable materials that will ignite with a single spark.

order.why: Read the account of warnings given to philosophers and learned audiences.
shortened: In brief, in all gatherings I cried out: O wise ones of the world! O philosophers of the West! O learned ones of the earth! A dark cloud approaches that shall envelop the horizon of humanity; a fierce tempest lurks behind, which shall shatter the ships of human life; and a mighty deluge shall soon overtake the cities and habitations of Europe.

order.why: Keep the retrospective relation between counsels and wartime events attributed.
Read the reported warning about a European war with its supplied date intact.
shortened: Universal War with its stupendous complications will ere long become an actuality and afflict the blind and heedless world with its awful consequences. This I say because Europe has become an arsenal filled with explosive materials and one of these days will set it aflame.

order.why: Keep the reported prediction involving Germany and France historically situated.
Read the reported expectation of changes in European political structures.
shortened: Tremendous changes will take place in Europe. The great centralized powers will break up into smaller independent states.

order.why: Keep the answer about the Rhine in its available question-and-answer context.
Read the reported companion warning about the Rhine and Berlin.
shortened: He said, 'O Banks of the River Rhine, blood shall flow in thee, because thou didst become negligent of God. Another war will come and blood will flow and there shall be lamentations in Berlin.'

order.why: Consider the source’s warning of another war after the previous one.
Read prayer for Germany’s peace beside the warning of further tribulations.
shortened: Your letter hath been received and I have implored fervently that that blessed community in Germany may grow and flourish day by day, and that through your endeavours Germany may be reborn and may receive the outpourings of grace from the realms on high, so that the whole country may gain peace and tranquillity in the years ahead, inasmuch as future events in Europe are fraught with tribulations.

order.why: Examine the stated persistence of self-interest during the Paris peace deliberations.
Keep the reported glimmer-of-dawn image for the postwar proposals.
Read the reported distinction between palliation and remedy.
Keep the reported warning about racial antagonism in its American setting.
shortened: If the races do not come to an agreement, there can be no question or doubt of bloodshed. When I was in America, I told the white and colored people that it was incumbent upon them to be united or else there would be the shedding of blood. I did not say more than this so that they might not be saddened. But, indeed, there is a greater danger than only the shedding of blood. It is the destruction of America.

order.why: Read the reported protest of subjects against rulers who expose them to war.
Consider the reported instability of apparently firm political arrangements.
Keep the source’s critique of attempted political remedies within its own setting.
shortened: Consider how they have tried every proposition - at times kindling the fire of independence, at times raising the banner of constitutionalism, one moment turning to the democratic party, another moment recognizing the unity party. From the beginning they eagerly pursued abrogated verses and insufficient proofs, but found no benefit and saw nothing but harm.

order.why: Read the ocean-and-gulfs image in its argument about fragmentation.
shortened: Consider the Law of the Apostle of God - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for His sake - as an ocean from which countless gulfs have been derived, and this hath caused the weakening of God's Law among His servants. To this day, neither kings nor subjects nor paupers have recognized the cause and reason, nor have they known how that which was lost in glory might be regained and the fallen standard might be raised again.

order.why: Consider apparent advancement accompanied by moral decline.
Read the source’s claim that the true physician is prevented from treating the world.
shortened: The world is in turmoil, and no soul hath comprehended its cause and reason. They have prevented the true Physician from healing these ailments, while they themselves know neither the malady nor its cure.

order.why: Explore the need for a remedy suited to the present illness.
shortened: It is clear and evident to every person of understanding that today the body of the world is ill with a chronic and severe malady - a skilled physician must necessarily treat it.
In former times the illness was of one kind, now it is of another kind.

order.why: Read the critique of contending physicians and a distressed patient.
shortened: The human world is sick and unconscious, and the physicians of morality are themselves in the utmost contention, having not yet discovered the cause of the illness - indeed, they are completely unaware. When you look to the truth, the physicians themselves are sicker, weaker and greedier than all others. Despite this, all the nations of the world are so heedless that they do not realize that except for the Divine Physician, in whose hands lies the constitution of the human world, none can cure these ills or provide the supreme remedy.

order.why: Consider the diseased body image for the condition of the world.
shortened: O ye lovers of God! The world is even as a human being who is diseased and impotent, whose eyes can see no longer, whose ears have gone deaf, all of whose powers are corroded and used up.

order.why: Keep the address to a spiritual physician amid many illnesses.
shortened: O spiritual physician! The weak body of the world is afflicted with a hundred thousand chronic, fatal diseases, and the ailing existence of humanity is exposed to great dangers, restless and suffering.

order.why: Read the image of visible and hidden wounds.
Preserve the brief reported diagnosis of a very sick world.
Consider the reported relation between materialism and diminished spiritual receptivity.
Keep the divine-physician analogy attributed to its theological setting.
Read the body’s coherent whole and the treatment of an ailing part.
shortened: And further, although the degrees of being are various, yet all are good. Observe the human body, its limbs, its members, the eye, the ear, the organs of smell, of taste, the hands, the fingernails. Notwithstanding the differences among all these parts, each one within the limitations of its own being participateth in a coherent whole. If one of them faileth it must be healed, and should no remedy avail, that part must be removed.

order.why: Consider the source’s lament over cruelty treated as virtue.
shortened: O friends! Black clouds have shrouded all this earth, and the darkness of hatred and malice, of cruelty and aggression and defilement is spreading far and wide. The people, one and all, live out their lives in a heedless stupor and the chief virtues of man are held to be his rapacity and his thirst for blood.

order.why: Read the storm and blood-drenched flood as images of widespread suffering.
shortened: O ye my loved ones! The world is wrapped in the thick darkness of open revolt and swept by a whirlwind of hate. It is the fires of malevolence that have cast up their flames to the clouds of heaven, it is a blood-drenched flood that rolleth across the plains and down the hills, and no one on the face of the earth can find any peace.

order.why: Keep the account of economic rivalry and military preparation together.
shortened: You behold multitudes racing in the arena of profit and loss, and waves of madness manifesting from all directions. Clamor rises high, and tumult and commotion reach every conscious ear. Strife and contention reign between every rich and poor, and warfare with sword and spear and bow and arrow between every lowly and noble one. Armies from every direction stand in battle array, and implements of fire from every quarter are arranged in order. The swords of hatred flash their brilliant gleam from afar, and the arrows of animosity pierce with their lightning-swift sharpness even in the darkest night, dazzling all eyes.

order.why: Read the battlefield imagery as a lament over abandoned human virtues.
Preserve the concise reported description of wartime chaos.
Read dark clouds as an image of enduring conflict.
shortened: In brief, very dark clouds have surrounded the horizon of the world. This is why you observe that all is war and strife, conflict and bloodshed. Humanity is in endless tribulation.

order.why: Consider the brief invitation to observe nations in turmoil.
shortened: Ye observe to what a degree the world is in continual turmoil and conflict, and to what a pass its nations have now come.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of collective despair.
shortened: O friends! All peoples and nations are frozen and lifeless, and all tribes and peoples are caught in despair and hopelessness.

order.why: Read distress, famine, drought, and upheaval together.
shortened: O thou who art stirred by the outpourings of the All-Merciful!

In the assemblage of the world there is a tremendous tumult, and intense agitation and distress, with cries and lamentations reaching to the zenith of heaven. There are moans and groans resounding through the highest heaven. There is anguish and affliction companion to every heart, and famine and drought prevailing in most countries of the world. There is turmoil and sedition in every region and territory.

order.why: Consider the direct indictment of destructive conduct.
shortened: O Rustam! The way of humankind today is oppression and tyranny, savagery and ferocity, bloodthirstiness and estrangement, corruption and injury.

order.why: Keep the severe animal imagery attributed to the source’s critique of war.
Read the reported darkness of hostility and religious antagonism.
Consider the reported coexistence of ignorance, enmity, and rumors of war.
shortened: At present the world is still very dark. From one side there threatens the darkness of ignorance; from another side black enmity is visible; from the other side we hear of war and rumors of war.

order.why: Read the source’s image of obscured spiritual light.
shortened: Thou art clearly observing how dismal and dark has grown the world of humanity, how the gloom of nature has surrounded all things and how the light of the kingdom has been utterly concealed.

order.why: Keep tyranny as the stated cause of repeated ordeals.
shortened: The world is seen to be in turmoil through the tyranny of the nations. Each day it is afflicted with a new ordeal and from every corner a tribulation arises.

order.why: Read the image of afflictions recurring in different places.
shortened: For many years afflictions have not ceased from the earth but rather pour forth like torrential rain. If they subside in one direction, they flame forth from another.

order.why: Join the companion torrent image to the source’s account of deeds and consequences.
shortened: These abominable deeds have been and will be the cause of tribulation and hardship for all on earth. For many years afflictions have not ceased from the earth, but flow like torrential rain. If they subside in one place, they flare up in another.

order.why: Consider how swiftly destruction undoes years of building.
Read the source’s account of Alexandria’s destruction within its historical setting.
shortened: Alexandria, which was adorned with all the ornaments of the world, was seen naked and bare within mere hours - nay rather, ruined and desolate. There is no power nor strength except in God. The recompense of deeds hath become embodied and assumed various forms. They flee, but there is no refuge; they cry for help, but it is not the time for help; they run, but there is no escape.

order.why: Keep the call to seek a remedy amid bombardment and bloodshed.
shortened: Thou hast witnessed and continueth to witness how each day a city among the cities of Islam falleth under the bombardment of cannons, and a faction among its factions faceth the bullets. That which hath appeared on earth hath caused the dwellers of the celestial realm to lament. Yet until now, none hath awakened or arisen to find a remedy.

order.why: Read the source’s numerical claim and warning against a narrowly local view.
shortened: Nearly twenty million souls perished, and in most regions of those parts blood flowed like rivers. Do not consider the world to be limited to one tract of land. Observe what hath befallen the servants in the vast renowned lands mentioned in the Books of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Consider the war’s losses across cities, households, and generations.
shortened: O my dear spiritual daughter! This recent terrible war was a catastrophe for the human world. It was like a flood that flows with utmost force from mountain peaks and uproots the foundations of all cities and villages.

Cities were overturned, villages were destroyed, properties were plundered, millions of souls were killed, households collapsed, millions of fathers lost their sons, millions of children became fatherless, and millions of women became destitute.

order.why: Read warfare on land, sea, air, and under water beside family suffering.
shortened: Until now, war was confined to land and sea, but in this age it extended to the heights of the sky and depths of the ocean. It became the great resurrection, and a supreme calamity occurred. Young children were left fatherless, and aged fathers lost their sons. Oppressed mothers wept blood, and loving sisters raised their voices in lamentation.

order.why: Keep the reported lament over battlefield deaths, plunder, and ruined homes.
shortened: In any case, in these days the fire of war in East and West sends its flames to the heavens. Millions of souls on the battlefield are mingled with dust and blood. How much wealth is plundered and pillaged! Millions of precious souls are afflicted with utter abasement. How many cities have been utterly destroyed from their foundations! How many homes have been and are being completely effaced and ruined! The human world has risen in bloodthirst; all, like wolves and leopards, tear each other apart and give no thought whatsoever to what the outcome of this bloodthirst will be.

order.why: Preserve the companion account separately with its own source identity.
Read the reported furnace image for lives sacrificed by rulers.
Keep the reported casualty estimate and description of collective shock attributed.
Read the reported warning that war inflicts wounds lasting centuries.
Consider the reported spread of warfare through whole populations.
Read the reported remorse of governments after reckless entry into war.
shortened: Now that the world is in turmoil, let us see what will happen after this tempest; God willing, it will turn out well. These governments, without remembering the difficulties of this war, or considering its consequences, or taking into account the gravity of the situation, rush recklessly into war. Now both sides are remorseful.

order.why: Consider the reported paralysis of international commerce.
shortened: East and West the affairs of the people are in utter confusion and the markets of the world are afflicted with lethargy. The wheels of international transactions are at a stand-still.

order.why: Read the intertwined losses of livelihoods, conscription, and family shelter.
shortened: Trade has become entirely non-existent and all the inhabitants are enlisted as soldiers. For example there are many merchants who have suffered complete ruin and to cap their misery they are compelled to enter the army and are sent to the frontier. Their wives and children are left behind without any helper, homeless and shelterless. Consider what a catastrophe is this!

order.why: Keep the reversals of wealth, rank, and sovereignty in their wartime setting.
Read the poetic image of universal exposure to affliction.
shortened: As for the current disorder in affairs, today the masses are in utmost upheaval and turmoil. As the poet says: "There is not a thorn's point that is not red with martyrs' blood." And the Turkish poet says: "In this azure dome there is not a shield; All atoms are targets for the arrows of fate."

order.why: Consider the recipient’s sorrow and interruption of planned public service.
Read compassion, grief, and prayer for a distressed nation.
Keep the concrete counsel about travel amid danger.
shortened: I have absolutely no time and am writing two brief words in reply that if travel and movement in the ports of the Persian Gulf is dangerous due to sedition, corruption and control by highway robbers, after achieving your purpose in those parts, proceed directly here.

order.why: Read the source’s testimony of protection without converting it into a general immunity claim.
shortened: The friends of God must observe that in this mighty tempest and severe turmoil that has afflicted all peoples of the world with utmost trials and tribulations - millions from noble houses and honored families became targets of bullets and swords, lives were lost, mighty edifices fell, young men rolled in dust and blood while loving fathers wept and dear mothers rent their garments and innocent children became helpless orphans, villages were leveled flat, cries and laments arose from all directions, losses and damages brought down the wealthy - despite all this turmoil and upheaval, the friends of God in every place remained safe and protected.

order.why: Keep the companion account of protection and lived teachings in its stated circumstances.
Read detachment and refuge in unity amid the world’s turmoil.
shortened: O friends who sacrifice their souls! The world is in turmoil and existence is in utmost hardship and endless tribulation, except for the friends of God who are birds of the nest of sanctity and doves in the garden of divine unity, detached from all else but God.

order.why: Preserve the acknowledgment of past protection and uncertainty about what follows.
shortened: Until now, despite severe storms and mighty waves, the Ship of the Cause has been preserved - let us see what God wills thereafter.

order.why: Read the prayer for protection amid cannons and drawn swords.
Consider the call to seek protection for others amid recurring upheaval.
shortened: After its perusal it was presented before His presence, whereupon He said: O thou who soarest in the atmosphere of love and gazest toward the horizon of grace! In this day it is incumbent upon all to seek protection from God, exalted be His glory, for His loved ones and chosen ones, inasmuch as commotions and upheavals have encompassed all. Each day a fresh calamity descendeth upon the world and a new sedition ariseth, yet none hath discovered the cause and reason thereof.

order.why: Read the contrast between anticipated revelation and inattentive response.
Consider altered perception as an obstacle to recognizing a remedy.
Keep the lament concerning the declining value accorded to religion.
Read the source’s account of increasing irreligion and an appointed duration.
Preserve the companion statement separately without imposing a calculated date.
shortened: Yea, the face of the world is turned toward irreligion. In all years, nay in all months, nay in all days, it is far from faith, knowledge and certitude, clinging to doubts and vain imaginings. And for a time it shall continue thus, even as its duration hath been revealed and recorded in God's Book.

order.why: Read the hope of gathering scattered letters amid a period of decline.
shortened: Indeed, the face of the world hath been turned toward irreligion. In all years, nay in all months, nay in all days, it hath been far from faith, certitude and knowledge, and close to conjecture and vain imaginings. For a time it shall continue thus, even as the duration thereof hath been revealed and recorded in the Book of God. But be not thou sorrowful, for the effulgences of the Sun of Truth shall assuredly absorb the superfluous moistures of nature and shall gather together the scattered letters.

order.why: Consider the source’s account of ignorance and the stilling of upheaval.
Read the image of vain imaginings seizing peoples.
shortened: O Muhammad-'Ali! The world is in upheaval. The darkness of the vain imaginings of the peoples hath seized them with the grasp of a tyrannical avenger.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of signs, heedlessness, and promised events.
shortened: The world's convulsions increase daily, yet its people perceive not the cause and reason, and remain veiled from what is with God by what is with themselves.

Most of what was revealed by the Supreme Pen in sacred texts and tablets hath come to pass, as thou hast witnessed, and what remaineth suspended in the heaven of God's Will shall assuredly be made manifest. Woe unto the heedless when the Great Terror comes!

order.why: Read the lament that repeated shocks have not awakened attention.
shortened: This year, calamities and blows of stagnation and corruption have encompassed all horizons, for the proof has been completed for all.

Despite this, people are still caught in the sleep of negligence, clinging to the metaphorical and shunning reality. People are still so immersed in carnal desires that even the trumpet of Israfil would not awaken them.

order.why: Consider the warning of later remorse for present neglect.
shortened: Soon you will observe that the ignorance of the heedless ones has become the cause of remorse, and the blindness of the ignorant ones the cause of misfortune, and from every direction will rise the cry "Oh, woe unto us for what we neglected towards God!"

order.why: Keep the brief statement about future moral degeneration in its own terms.
shortened: In a time to come, morals will degenerate to an extreme degree. It is essential that children be reared in the Baha'i way, that they may find happiness both in this world and the next. If not, they shall be beset by sorrows and troubles, for human happiness is founded upon spiritual behavior.

order.why: Read the reported account of classes, revolution, and civilizational destruction as a pilgrim-era claim.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty has plainly written that there will be revolutions and disturbances. There are three classes. High-or educated-- middle and low classes, this (lower) class are dominating. The common classes will dominate and that will be revolution. Irreligion will prevail and at the end the whole civilization of the world will be destroyed.

order.why: Keep the reported rocking-cradle image of failed awakening.
shortened: These are God-sent calamities for man so that people will grow repentant and contrite. However, these people are like children in the cradle, the more you rock them, the sleepier they get. The affairs of men have been thrown in confusion in both the East and the West.

order.why: Read the reported connection between neglect of teachings and disorder.
Keep the reported language of wrath and retribution attributed to its wartime account.
Read the source’s account of wartime distress and promised calamity.
shortened: However, due to the war that has occurred, the people of these regions are in distress and afflicted with utmost hardship. All ears are heedless of the call of the muezzin, and hearts are empty of the knowledge and love of Truth. In brief, a great calamity hath encompassed the people. This is what the All-Merciful promised in the Tablets.

order.why: Consider the Hidden Words’ warning concerning deeds and accountability.
Read the warning’s conditional summons to turn toward God.
Keep the source’s sequence of agitation, appointed hour, and renewed standard.
shortened: The world is in travail, and its agitation waxeth day by day. Its face is turned towards waywardness and unbelief. Such shall be its plight, that to disclose it now would not be meet and seemly. Its perversity will long continue. And when the appointed hour is come, there shall suddenly appear that which shall cause the limbs of mankind to quake. Then, and only then, will the Divine Standard be unfurled, and the Nightingale of Paradise warble its melody.

order.why: Read the promise of justice within its warning against corruption.
shortened: The day is approaching when the wrathful anger of the Almighty will have taken hold of them. He, verily, is the Omnipotent, the All-Subduing, the Most Powerful. He shall cleanse the earth from the defilement of their corruption, and shall give it for an heritage unto such of His servants as are nigh unto Him.

order.why: Consider love as a spiritual resource amid fear.
shortened: Let His love be a storehouse of treasure for your souls, on the Day when naught else but Him shall profit you, the Day when every pillar shall tremble, when the very skins of men shall creep, when all eyes shall stare up with terror.

order.why: Keep the source’s language of terror and deliverance.
shortened: This is the Day on which all eyes shall stare up with terror, the Day in which the hearts of them that dwell on earth shall tremble, save them whom thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, pleaseth to deliver.

order.why: Read the warning concerning Baghdad and the treatment of captives in its addressed setting.
shortened: Soon will the land of Baghdad be changed, and that which is outside it, and it shall pass out of the hands of the King, and commotions shall appear, and the voice of lamentation shall be raised, and corruption shall become manifest on all sides, and affairs shall be disrupted by reason of that which hath befallen these captives at the hands of the hosts of oppression. The established order shall be changed, and conditions shall wax so grievous that the very sands on the desolate hills will moan, and the trees on the mountain will weep, and blood will flow out of all things, and thou shalt behold the people in sore distress."

order.why: Records a warning concerning upheaval in the Land of Mystery.
Consider forewarning intended to sustain steadfastness.
shortened: Mention has been made of the grievous days [ayyam-i-shidad] in the Tablet of Steadfastness. The Truth has informed all in wondrous and sublime Tablets of the great tribulation, that perchance the people might not be perturbed when it comes to pass, and might not be debarred from the path of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Read the companion purpose of warning as preparation against agitation.
shortened: Most of the friends have been seized with agitation due to the tribulation of these grievous days, though We had informed them of it beforehand so that they might not be agitated but rather be among the steadfast ones.

order.why: Keep the stated relation between upheaval and revelation within the source’s theological account.
shortened: O ye friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! The tumult of the nations and the clamour of their peoples are certain and inevitable in the Day of the Manifestation of the Most Great Name. The wisdom of this irrevocable decree is clear and evident.

order.why: Read the language of successive convulsions without creating an editorial timetable.
shortened: The foundations of the Concourse on high were shaken when the Call was raised from the Supreme Horizon, and thou seest the people reeling from the great quaking that hath caused all the powers of the earth to tremble, and which shall be followed by a mightier convulsion, more bitter and terrible.

order.why: Keep the year of shidad and its imagery in the source’s stated form.
shortened: All these tribulations and calamities, difficulties and afflictions are from the effects and requirements of this year of shidad, for the most great convulsion has appeared and the greatest resurrection has arisen. In such a mighty tempest one cannot imagine a shore of rest and deliverance.

order.why: Preserve the source’s number without silently converting its calendar or interpretation.
Read the prayer’s conjunction of new creation and a severe age.
Consider the source’s connection between scriptural imagery and cannons.
Read ingathering, justice, and fire within the Tablet’s address.
Consider revelation as shaking creation and disclosing mysteries.
shortened: And when the hour at which Thy resistless Faith was to be made manifest did strike, Thou didst breathe a breath of Thy spirit into Thy Pen, and lo, the entire creation shook to its very foundations, unveiling to mankind such mysteries as lay hidden within the treasuries of Him Who is the Possessor of all created things."

order.why: Read the disruption of equilibrium through a new order.
Keep the concise promise of a changed order.
shortened: Soon will the present-day order be rolled up, and a new one spread out in its stead. Verily, thy Lord speaketh the truth, and is the Knower of things unseen.

order.why: Read the companion statement of a new order separately.
Preserve the source’s fragmentary wording and remembrance of divine sovereignty.
Keep the reported account of universal interconnection and consequences of actions.
shortened: Question: Are great calamities like this flood, the San Francisco earthquake, etc., caused by the wickedness of the people?

Answer: It belongs to the lesson of yesterday. Events like these happen because of the connection between the parts of the universe, for every small part has connection with every great part, and what affects one affects the other or all others.
On account of this connection, the actions of man have effect. Whenever a promise is broken, it causes a commotion.

order.why: Read the reported interpretation of verses as worldwide struggle.
shortened: The first and second verses mean that an unheard of gen[eral] revolution and struggle shall occur in the world which will be a manifest calamity to all mankind. This catastrophe will bring in its train mu[ch] sufferings and trials.

order.why: Keep the reported numerical predictions and casualty assertions clearly tied to their conversation.
Read the reported admission that future changes exceed present imagination.
Consider the reported theater image for changing human affairs.
Read the reported concern over collective forgetfulness after upheaval.
shortened: Historians of each country, no doubt, will marshal the salient events of this tremendous struggle for the benefit of the reading public, but the public as a mass of men are indifferent, heedless, whimsical and forgetful. Theirs is not the royal minds of the few to grasp the general bearings of these world-shaking earthquakes.

order.why: Keep the reported expectation of wisdom becoming visible afterward.
Read the reported association between wartime circumstances and the Tablets.
shortened: One of the wisdoms of this universal war is no other than the writing of these Epistles, so that the believers may realize that the Cause of his Holiness Baha'u'llah must ultimately encircle the globe.

order.why: Consider the call to renewed service after wartime interruption.
shortened: In any case, the years of upheaval and intense anxiety, whatever they were, have passed. Now that calm and assurance have been attained, one must charge forth like a fierce lion and valiant hero in the arena of sacrifice, for through this sudden war humankind has developed an intense receptivity, and the loftiness of divine teachings, the luminosity of divine laws, and the contents of divine tablets have been realized.

order.why: Read education and spiritual teachings amid the account of prejudice in the East.
shortened: In the journal write thus:
When the horizon of the East was covered with immense darkness; when dark clouds were predominate, and when all the heavenly stars were concealed to the eye.

The light of that Sun of Reality consisted of heavenly teachings which were spread in the Orient, because there the obscurities of blind imitations, of religious, sectarian, racial, political, economic and home prejudices were in ascendency. The darkness of these prejudices had dominated the Oriental world to such a degree that it has blinded all the eyes and deafened all the ears. There prevailed quarrel and strife, warfare and bloodshed.

order.why: Keep the companion historical framing in its own source voice.
shortened: The approach should be this:  that the horizon of the East had become very dark and illumination was entirely lost. The dust of prejudice had so encompassed all that all the peoples of the East were in the utmost hatred and enmity with each other, and were entirely deprived of human virtues and heavenly civilization, even physical civilization.

order.why: Read the reported call to act as nurses and doctors alongside its distinct expectations.
shortened: There is suffering everywhere. The world is a huge hospital, and souls are crying in the dark. The world is a huge battlefield, and the Holy Spirit is flooding every spot; but the souls are dead or dying. The Bahais should be nurses and doctors.

The time as prophesied from all time is short - very short. How is the Holy Spirit to be recognised by the world? A great mass of people all over the world who have united as brothers in sorrow, suffering and affliction, will be persecuted until their cries reach the very gates of heaven. Then Angels of Light will arise and these people will receive the Message I came to bring and have held so long, waiting for more sorrow and suffering.

order.why: Consider the prayer that suffering might become the pains of a new birth.
Read hope for peace, unity, and the spread of teachings after war.
shortened: We hope that hereafter eyes shall become seeing and ears hearing, and the standard of human unity shall wave at the pole of the horizons, and the pavilion of universal peace shall cast its shade upon East and West. The Blessed Tree shall grow and develop, and the counsels and admonitions of the Blessed Beauty shall spread. It is certain that after this war, these teachings shall raise their banner in every clime, and this life-giving breeze shall set the world in motion.

order.why: Keep the reported statement of peace following upheaval.
shortened: This peace will come about after great upheavals and events take place.

order.why: Read the hope for clouds to disperse and tranquility to return.
Close the linked readings with restoration and the removal of calamity’s foundations.
Open supplied readings with the explicit caution against predicting comets or other unsupported natural disasters.
Read the warning that Bahais also share suffering and responsibility.
shortened: In such a process of purgation, when all humanity is in the throes of dire suffering, the Baha'is should not hope to remain unaffected. Should we consider the beam that is in our own eye, we would immediately find that these sufferings are also meant for ourselves, who claimed to have attained. Such world crisis is necessary to awaken us to the importance of our duty and the carrying on of our task.

order.why: Keep the supplied convulsion passage with its distinct catalogue status.
Read the supplied collection of warnings with its composite citation intact.
shortened: "O ye peoples of the world! Know, verily, that an unforeseen calamity is following you, and that grievous retribution awaiteth you. Think not the deeds ye have committed have been blotted from My sight."         "O heedless ones! Though the wonders of My mercy have encompassed all created things, both visible and invisible, and though the revelations of My grace and bounty have permeated every atom of the universe, yet the rod with which I can chastise the wicked is grievous, and the fierceness of Mine anger against them terrible."

order.why: Keep the severe numerical and population claims explicitly attributed to pilgrim notes.
Preserve both supplied pilgrim-note versions without granting them added authority.
Read the supplied diagnosis of materialism with its unresolved source ending retained.
shortened: The universal crisis affecting mankind is, therefore, essentially spiritual in its causes. The spirit of the age, taken on the whole, is irreligious. Man's outlook on life is too crude and materialistic to enable him to elevate himself into the higher realms of the spirit.
