It is this condition, so sadly morbid, into which society has fallen, that religion seeks to improve and transform...

order.why: Consider the supplied questions concerning suffering and the establishment of a new order.
Read the supplied account of disintegration and the vision of an organic commonwealth.
shortened: The process of disintegration must inexorably continue, and its corrosive influence must penetrate deeper and deeper into the very core of a crumbling age. Much suffering will still be required ere the contending nations, creeds, classes and races of mankind are fused in the crucible of universal affliction, and are forged by the fires of a fierce ordeal into one organic commonwealth, one vast, unified, and harmoniously functioning system.

order.why: Keep the supplied institutional letter’s account of suffering and unification.
Read the supplied promise of justice after upheaval.
Keep the supplied expectation of universal regeneration within its dated letter.
shortened: But, what is needed nowadays is a universal regeneration resulting from an intense universal suffering. It is not sufficient that only a portion of humanity may become conscious of the needs of the time. The masses must be awakened from their deep slumber. And nothing can achieve that except the fire of a world-wide ordeal. The Guardian is praying that this hour of victory may approach, and that upon the ruins of the old the new World Order of the Faith may be safely and completely established.

order.why: Consider the supplied contrast between passing arrangements and enduring institutions.
Read the supplied expectation of future growth without creating a schedule.
Keep communal maturity beside social disintegration as the two stated factors.
Read the supplied image of creation shaken by a divine summons.
Turn toward the supplied appeal to help a suffering world.
Read the call to persevere amid rising calamity and despair.
Close with serene, confident, unremitting assistance according to one’s circumstances.

questions: What changes when the human costs of war are placed at the center of reading about calamity?
How do the passages connect destructive events with prejudice, rivalry, self-interest, and collective choices?
How should the source, date, and authority of a passage shape the way its warnings or predictions are understood?
What relationships do the images of illness, storms, and childbirth suggest between suffering and the possibility of renewal?
How does Jesus’ response in Luke challenge assumptions about victims while directing attention toward the listener’s own responsibility?
What forms of education, reconciliation, care, or service could give practical expression to the hope for peace in these readings?

references.label: 1 · Luke 13:1–5 · Disaster and the listener’s responsibility
references.note: Read Jesus’ response to accounts of people killed by violence and by a falling tower. He rejects the inference that the victims were worse sinners, while calling His listeners to repentance. Compare this turn toward the listener with the compilation’s demands for moral change and service. How can reflection on calamity deepen responsibility and compassion?

subjects.displayTitle: The divine encounter: presence, recognition, and nearness
subjects.introduction: To enter the presence of God, Bahá’u’lláh writes, is to open the eye of justice and know the Truth by the Truth with a pure heart. The Báb explains that no one encounters the Essence itself, so every scriptural promise of meeting the Lord points to the Sun of Reality that rises on the Day of Resurrection, and he bears witness that to meet Him is to meet God. The encounter then becomes intimate: a gate thrown open, a voice heard at the door of the prison in ‘Akká, a single hour in that presence worth more than sovereignty over heaven and earth. Those forbidden to come are promised the reward of the meeting they longed for, and a grieving son hears that his mother, who attained that court, lives on. Philip’s plea to be shown the Father, and the answer that turns him back to the one before him, keeps the question alive in another tongue. From here the way leads into the Manifestation as mediator and sole route to knowing God, and into prayer for nearness and reunion.
subjects.arc: Begin with recognition, justice, and nearness beyond distance; explore the theology of meeting and revelation; follow invitations, visits, and their obstacles; then move through remembrance, bereavement, and prayers for reunion.

order.why: Open with justice and a pure heart as a station of presence.
Place belief in the verses beside the limits of physical nearness.
Consider an assurance of presence even when the recipient was unaware.
shortened: Grieve not at separation, for We have brought thee into the presence of the Throne while thou wert heedless thereof.

order.why: Read the prayer that those who turn receive the reward of meeting.
shortened: O Lord! Ordain for every soul who turns toward Thee that which Thou hast ordained for those who have attained Thy presence, visited Thy Beauty, and heard Thy verses after ears were forbidden from hearing them.

order.why: Explore the Bab’s explicit distinction between the inaccessible Essence and the Sun of Reality.
shortened: For there is no doubt that the encounter with the very Essence is impossible; rather, in the primordial reality, what is intended is the meeting with the Sun of Reality, and thereafter, in the mode of semblance, with those who point unto it -- the Names of God, exalted and glorified -- together with the guides unto the Point upon the day of its Manifestation.

Know thou that the Presentation is not unto the Essence of Eternity, for nothing can reach unto It. Rather, the Presentation is the presentation unto the Tree of Truth on the Day of Resurrection, which is the presentation unto God in the Primal Reality.

order.why: Read the scriptural question concerning vision and the contrasting interpretations it raises.
shortened: Despite these explicit statements, clear texts, and inherited traditions, the peoples have differed on this question. Some have said that vision is impossible, citing the blessed verse: "No vision can grasp Him, but His grasp is over all vision: He is above all comprehension, yet is acquainted with all things." Others have said that to wholly deny vision would necessitate denial of Qur'anic texts and disprove the infallibility of the Prophets, for to ask for that which is impossible is categorically impermissible for an infallible Prophet. Moses the Interlocutor--peace be upon Him--asked for vision, saying: "O my Lord! Show me Thyself that I may look upon Thee."

order.why: Hear the affirmation that all are allotted the station of meeting.
Consider the value placed on a single encounter.
Read the Bab’s account of meeting the promised One while affirming divine incomprehensibility.
shortened: I bear witness, O my God, that to meet Him is to meet Thee, for Thou canst not be comprehended in Thine Essence nor seen in Thy Reality, and there existeth not in Thy creation any mirror Thou mightest choose for Thine Essence wherein naught can be seen save Thee and which pointeth to none other than Thee.

order.why: Explore revelation as the way creation knows and praises God.
Keep the Bab’s subtle language of witnessing free from likeness and division.
shortened: And whoso visiteth God through God's witnessing of His own Self unto Himself hath entered the Gate of Grandeur, and hath been a visitor of the Lord of Might upon the dust -- without knowing even a trace of likeness, nor a letter of similitude, nor a name of delineation, nor a description of division. For God hath ever been, and there was nothing with Him; and description belonged only to that which doth not indicate itself by itself, and attribution is valid only for that which doth not know itself by itself.

order.why: Read the concise identification of meeting with the manifestation of the Self.
Preserve the companion statement of meeting and veiling.
shortened: He is God, there is no God but Him, from a beginning that hath no beginning unto an end that hath no end, and all are promised to attain His presence. And this indeed is the meeting with the Manifestation of His Self, yet the servants remain veiled.

order.why: Read the meeting described as the enrichment that matters.
Consider the call to recognize the promised manifestation beyond limiting conditions.
Read the language of revelation to all things through signs of oneness and mercy.
Keep the Bab’s address to Sayyah and its language of service and presence in context.
Read the reported explanation of Moses’ request, retaining its rejection of bodily incarnation.
Keep the reported account of differing Muslim interpretations attributed to its source.
Read the reported phrase about meeting God with its own authority distinct.
shortened: It is said: " O people, you will meet God in the Flesh, you will visit him."

order.why: Consider the identification of turning toward the Manifestation with turning toward God.
shortened: Say: Whoso turneth away from Me hath turned away from God from all eternity, and whoso gazeth upon Me hath gazed upon God, the Generous, the Forgiving.

order.why: Read the companion account of attachment, turning, and rejection.
shortened: Whoso holdeth fast unto Him hath held fast unto God, and whoso turneth unto Him hath turned unto the Most Sublime Horizon, and whoso turneth away from Him hath turned away from God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Keep the concise relation between knowing Him and knowing God.
shortened: And He Who speaketh with truth is verily the Ocean of My Will and the Heaven of My Purpose and the Rain of My Grace and the Sun of My Loving-kindness and the Repository of My Revelation and the Dayspring of My Inspiration and the Dawning-Place of My Cause and the Treasury of My Knowledge and the Source of My Salsabil and the Fountain of My Kawthar.
Whoso hath known Him hath known Me and whoso hath denied Him hath denied Me from time immemorial.

order.why: Read turning as beholding and receiving loving-kindness.
Explore recognition, obedience, remembrance, and presence as connected responses.
shortened: Verily he who hath turned unto Him hath turned unto My direction and appeared before My throne and heard My call and responded to My utterance and followed My commandments and attained My presence and drunk the choice wine of My favors and the Kawthar of My bounties and tasted the sweetness of My remembrance and My words and reached the ultimate goal in My Kingdom and My dominion.

order.why: Consider the Face through which faces turn toward the Worshipped One.
Read the stated station of the revealer and source of verses.
Hear the declaration of the Day of Meeting.
shortened: This is the Day of Meeting, for God hath appeared unveiled and manifest.

order.why: Read the hidden treasure becoming manifest and promised things fulfilled.
shortened: He is the One Who is manifest without veil or covering.

That which was hidden from time immemorial hath been revealed, and that which was treasured in God's knowledge, the Lord of lords, hath appeared, and that which was promised in the Books of God, the Master of necks, hath come to pass.

order.why: Consider the movement from inability to see to an invitation to behold.
shortened: The first Word that appeared from the Dawning-place of utterance of the Lord of Oneness was "Thou shalt not see Me," but now He saith "Behold and thou shalt see Me."

order.why: Read the identification of turning with seeing.
Hear the invitation to behold the manifested countenance.
shortened: Behold ye the countenance of God, the Lord of all worlds! He hath appeared from the most exalted horizon after the passing away of all things.

order.why: Consider the universal proclamation of what had been hidden.
shortened: All things speak, and behind them the Dawning-Place of Names proclaimeth between earth and heaven: "By God! The Hidden hath appeared and the Treasured One hath been revealed. Beware lest ye deprive yourselves of meeting with God, the Mighty, the Wise."

order.why: Read the unveiled countenance and illumination of horizons.
Keep the brief image of a rent veil and attraction.
Read the disclosure of what had lain hidden before nations.
Consider turning toward the countenance as the stated purpose of creation.
Keep the source’s contrast between creation’s purpose and its response.
Read the companion account of longing followed by rejection.
Consider the difference between recognizing a time and recognizing its spiritual meaning.
shortened: Some did not recognize the days of the Spirit, and some, through their own heedlessness, remained veiled from the knowledge and presence of the Beloved even after recognizing the days of God.

order.why: Read the warning that ascetic status does not itself ensure encounter.
Keep the brief warning concerning self-deprivation.
Read the source’s distinction between attaining and turning away.
shortened: Whosoever hath attained His presence on this Day, he is of the people of Baha in the Book of God, the Lord of the Final End. And whoso hath turned away, he is accounted among the people of error in the Scriptures and Tablets.

order.why: Consider inward turning as participation in the Day and presence.
shortened: Whoso turns to Him has attained unto the Day of God and His presence, and whoso turns away is accounted among the deprived ones.

order.why: Hear the appeal to learned people to open their eyes.
Read freedom from veils and transient means as an approach to lasting bounty.
shortened: How excellent is the state of that soul who today has not been prevented by the veils of the people of the world from the Most Great Ocean and the recognition of the Pre-existent Lord, and whom transient means have not deprived of everlasting bounties. With perfect certitude and assurance they have turned toward the Beloved of all creation and become vocal in His praise.

order.why: Consider meditation and inward hearing as a way toward the encounter.
shortened: Say: O people of the earth, hearken unto the divine call on this luminous Day, and meditate upon His Cause, and with the ear of your innate nature hear that which hath been sent down from the heaven of His Will, that haply ye may attain unto your goal and be blessed with His presence.

order.why: Read outer and inner hearing together.
shortened: The Call of God is raised from the direction of Akka, saying: "Blessed is he who hath turned unto God and hath hearkened with both outer and inner ear to His divine call." Such souls are the people of the Most Great Vista and the partakers of the Most Pure Wine - especially those who, in these days when the darkness of vain imaginings hath seized most of mankind, have not been hindered from turning toward the Court of Oneness.

order.why: Keep the Tablet of Visitation’s statement concerning its words and meeting.
shortened: Whoso visiteth what hath been sent down from the direction of the Throne in this Tablet and findeth himself in doubt concerning the meeting with his Lord - he is of them that have turned away from God, the Cleaver of the dawn.

order.why: Consider the messages, glad tidings, and return described in the source.
shortened: In them is that which will make men independent of all who are in the heavens and on earth, and will convey unto them the messages of God, and give them the glad-tidings of their meeting with the Self of God Who standeth over all created things, and warn them of the Day whereon all shall return unto God in a holy and gracious station.

order.why: Read the glad tidings of presence arising from imprisonment.
shortened: This is the Day wherein the Call hath been raised from the prison of 'Akka, and hath given the glad-tidings unto all peoples of the presence of God, the Lord of Lords.

order.why: Keep the summons amid sorrow and trials in its historical setting.
shortened: I swear by the Sun of Revelation that hath risen above the horizon of the prison that, at a time when sorrows had encompassed Us from all directions and trials and tribulations were pouring down like torrential rain, We summoned the peoples of the earth to the Most Exalted Horizon with all Our power and might.

order.why: Hear the call to announce the Day and the coming of the Lord of Names.
shortened: Arise to make mention and say: O people! The Day hath come and the call hath been raised betwixt earth and heaven. The Lord of Names hath come with manifest sovereignty.

order.why: Read the call’s letter imagery without supplying an invented explanation.
Consider the linked prophetic images of hearing, ascent, and understanding.
shortened: By God's life! Moses heard from it "Verily, there is none other God but I, the Mighty, the All-Wise," and Abraham hastened with his heart unto it and cried, "Yea, yea, O Beloved of them that know!" And the Friend ascended and soared on the wings of understanding to the Kingdom of the All-Merciful, the station wherein he beheld My greatest signs and heard My sweetest call.

order.why: Read the personal encounter through the memory of Moses and the Tree.
Keep the Day of Meeting, Sinai, and the cup of camphor together.
shortened: O thou who hast attained to the supreme bounty! On the Day of Meeting, on the Day of Manifestation, thou didst attain the honor of presence before Him Who was revealed on Sinai, and didst drink from the pure cup whose mixture was of camphor.

order.why: Read the light of Sinai as the source’s image for received revelation.
shortened: O ye servants of the Blessed Perfection!
In the Day of the Manifestation, you have caught the lights from the Manifestor on the Mount of Sinai and beheld the splendor of the Ray of Truth.

order.why: Consider the joy of creation at the appearance of the Speaker on Sinai.
shortened: O My leaves and My handmaidens! Today the divine breeze is passing by and the Spirit of God is in motion and manifestation. All things, with utmost joy and excitement, are delighted by the appearance of Him Who conversed on Sinai.

order.why: Read the extended birth-month imagery of creation rejoicing.
Keep the personified hill and spot of encounter in their setting.
shortened: This is a Day wherein the divine Hill hath attained the presence of God and the call hath been raised from all things: The Spot hath been adorned through the advent of the Lord of all beings.

order.why: Consider the garden’s personified joy at the arrival of the Beauty.
shortened: I am seeing through the horizon of knowledge:

O people of the earth! We desired the garden, and when We established Ourselves therein upon the throne, We heard it cry out and say: "O thrones of the world, rejoice ye, for the Beauty of the Ancient One hath been established upon me.

order.why: Read the prayer’s perception of the Beloved in city and garden.
Keep the hope of perceiving beauty and majesty wherever one looks.
Hear the concise declaration of the open gate.
Read the opened gate accompanied by the nightingales of utterance.
Consider the invitation to enter with illumined hearts.
shortened: The gate of meeting hath been opened and the Dayspring of Names proclaimeth: Enter ye with illumined hearts, O people of insight!

order.why: Read the longing of the sincere and the chosen for the station of meeting.
shortened: The matter which takes precedence over all things and the cause which transcends all causes hath been recorded in the Book by the Most Bountiful Pen as being the station of meeting with God. All those who have drawn nigh, the sincere ones, the pure ones and the chosen ones have longed for this most holy, most exalted and most glorious station.

order.why: Keep the recipient’s desire in relation to the purpose of creation.
Read the account of prayerful longing for the presence of revelation.
shortened: Night and day all people would beseech and supplicate with utmost humility and imploration the Self-Sufficient, the Exalted, yearning and hoping to attain the presence of the Manifestation of the divine Revelation and the Dawning-Place of the heavenly inspiration.

order.why: Consider the attraction of verses and longing for God.
shortened: By God! He who is drawn to the verses of his Lord will, out of his longing for God, the Mighty, the Praised One, abandon all creation.

order.why: Read the call to turn beyond created things toward the Beloved.
shortened: At all times must man pass beyond all created things and, turning his gaze toward God, his gracious Lord, hasten to the dwelling-place of the Beloved.

order.why: Consider the counsel about what to seek through prayer.
Read the Bab’s prayer valuing a moment of beauty above sovereignty.
shortened: Number me, O my God, with those who are privileged to fix their gaze upon Thy Beauty and who take such delight therein that they would not exchange a single moment thereof with the sovereignty of the kingdom of heavens and earth or with the entire realm of creation.

order.why: Keep hearing one melody and entering the holy place together.
shortened: By God! To hear but one melody from the mouth of God is better than all that hath been treasured in the heavens and earth, and thy entry into the Spot of God is better for thee than whatsoever hath been created on earth - and God is witness unto this.

order.why: Read the prayer of self-offering through the Manifestations.
shortened: By the glory of Thy might, O Thou my Well-Beloved! To have sacrificed my life for the Manifestations of Thy Self, to have offered up my soul in the path of the Revealers of Thy wondrous Beauty, is to have sacrificed my spirit for Thy Spirit, my being for Thy Being, my glory for Thy glory.

order.why: Consider the Bab’s instruction concerning reverence and permission in the presence.
shortened: When the Day-Star of Baha will shine resplendent above the horizon of eternity it is incumbent upon you to present yourselves before His Throne. Beware lest ye be seated in His presence or ask questions without His leave.

order.why: Read the expressed desire to meet friends in the outward realm.
Keep the source’s welcome of companionship and nearness.
Read the mutual longing to see, hear, and meet despite obstructing circumstances.
shortened: However, "We would not exchange meeting you for anything else." Would that you were present and saw and heard and knew, and we saw and heard and found. If only the preventing circumstances by divine decree were removed and meeting became possible.

order.why: Consider the expressed wish for companionship interrupted by others.
Read longing alongside the requirements of wisdom.
Keep the stated prohibition of a visit for reasons of wisdom.
shortened: The Friend hath come for the sake of meeting, and this matter hath been recorded as the greatest of deeds in the divine Books, yet due to wisdom it hath been forbidden.

order.why: Read the reward of intention when approach is not permitted.
Consider the acknowledgment of someone prevented from visiting.
Read the prayer of longing obstructed by oppression.
shortened: Say: O my God and my Lord! I have desired the waters of Thy presence and the wine of reunion with Thee, and to enter beneath the shade of the Tree of Thy oneness, and to stand before the Dayspring of Thy Cause and the Manifestation of Thy signs, yet have I been prevented therefrom by reason of what the hands of the oppressors among Thy creatures and the rebellious ones among Thy people have wrought.

order.why: Keep the source’s gratitude and subsequent prevention in its selected context.
shortened: O Most Holy, Most Glorious!
Praise be unto Thee, O my God, for having blessed Thy servant whom Thou didst honor with Thy presence and caused to hear Thy verses.
Thus was he prevented from attaining Thy presence.

order.why: Read the promise of the reward of meeting to one who desires it.
Consider forgiveness, joy, and the recorded reward of presence.
shortened: He is indeed the All-Bountiful, the Most Generous. He hath forgiven thee as a token of His grace and hath written down for thee, by His Most Exalted Pen, the reward of attaining His presence, that thou mayest rejoice and be among the thankful ones.

order.why: Read the prayer for those deprived of the outward meeting.
shortened: O Lord! Ordain for him and for Thy servants who have been deprived of meeting Thee the reward of those who have attained Thy presence and arranged an assembly for Thy name and remembrance.

order.why: Consider turning with one’s whole being and asking the reward of reunion.
shortened: O my Lord! I have turned to Thee with my whole being and I beseech Thee by Thy Self to ordain for me the reward of one who hath attained Thy presence, been honored to meet Thee, and drunk the choice wine of life from the ocean of reunion with Thee.

order.why: Read the prayer linking the desired reward to prophetic promises.
Keep the brief request for the reward of presence.
shortened: Then write down for me, O my God, by Thy Most Exalted Pen, the reward of attaining Thy presence and what Thou hast ordained for Thy chosen ones.

order.why: Remember the personal meeting with the Wronged One.
Read entry into the precincts by permission.
Consider the testimony that the recipient has been remembered and present.
Keep the source’s assurance of being seen and mentioned.
Read gratitude for presence before the object of divine favor.
Preserve the identification of the first arrival at the Most Great Prison.
shortened: Thou art the first one to attain the divine presence in His Most Great Prison.

order.why: Read the journey into prison and hearing the call.
Consider the remembered days of outward sight and hearing in prison.
Keep the testimony to entry into prison and meeting the Wronged One.
Keep the remembered letter and the Most Great Scene in their addressed setting.
Read the recipient’s meeting and hearing within the prison setting.
Consider arrival by permission and hearing the speaking Tree.
shortened: A mention from His presence unto him who has turned to the Most Great Prison by God's leave, the Lord of antiquity, and attained to that Spot round which circle the Concourse on High and the dwellers of the cities of names, and heard the call of the Tree which speaks at all times: "There is none other God but Him, the Mighty, the Bestower."

order.why: Read sight, hearing, verses, and promises as aspects of the encounter.
shortened: O thou who art present before the Countenance! We bear witness that thou didst hear the Call from the Supreme Horizon and didst turn unto it and attain unto the presence of the Wronged One and didst hear the shrill voice of His Pen and didst behold the horizon of His Revelation and didst gain that which was recorded in His Books and Scriptures and Tablets.

order.why: Keep the particular visit of father and brother during revelation of verses.
shortened: Thy father and thy brother came into the presence of the Countenance on a certain night, and heard the call of God, the Lord of the worlds, and arrived at an hour when the Tongue of Grandeur was speaking forth perspicuous verses and when all atoms were proclaiming: The dominion belongeth unto God, the Goal of all mystic knowers.

order.why: Read leaving a homeland and arriving at the place of revelation.
Consider the journey over land and sea toward the desired encounter.
Read migration, hearing, and the blessing of meeting together.
Keep the named recipient’s hearing and standing before the Pen.
Read repeated presence as a bounty prompting praise.
shortened: O Abdullah! Praise the Countenance of the Intended One, for through His bounty thou hast attained unto the Most Great Sea and time after time hast been honored to attain the presence of the Lord of Eternity.

order.why: Preserve the companion testimony of repeated encounter.
shortened: He testifies that you have turned to the Most Exalted Horizon and have attained the Kawthar of the presence time and again.

order.why: Consider visiting, belief, and the cup of bounty.
shortened: We bear witness that thou didst visit the Most Great Scene and didst believe in God, the Lord of destiny, and didst drink the most pure wine from the hand of the bounty of thy Lord, the All-Informed.

order.why: Read the opened door and fulfillment of promises in a personal address.
shortened: Thou didst arrive at the shore of the Most Great Ocean and didst hear the call of the Lord of Eternity, and didst enter through a door that was opened unto the faces of all who are in the heavens and the earth. Blessed art thou for having drunk, from the hands of bounty, the Kawthar of the divine encounter, and for having attained that which was recorded in the Books of the Prophets and Messengers.

order.why: Keep permission and the waters of reunion together.
Read the personal turning toward the Dayspring and its grace.
shortened: A mention from Us to one who turned to God and attained the presence when the Dayspring of the Cause appeared with a sovereignty that encompassed all created things, and who drank the choice wine of reunion when the Sun of the Beauty of his Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower, dawned from the horizon of grace.

order.why: Consider the testimony to a response amid others’ rejection.
shortened: We bear witness that he attained the presence of God in His days and appeared before the Throne and heard His call when every stubborn misbeliever turned away.

order.why: Read the personal encounter in relation to the purpose of beings.
shortened: Thou art among those souls who have attained unto His presence and reached this Most Great Cause, which hath been the purpose of the creation of all beings.

order.why: Distinguish visitation of the House and the Lord of the House in the source’s own terms.
Read meeting and forgiveness as freely bestowed gifts.
Keep the concise testimony of reunion from the hand of bounty.
Read the speaker’s testimony of presenting, hearing, and attaining.
Consider presence joined to the cup of inner meanings.
shortened: Blessed art thou, O servant, in that thou hast attained the presence of God and drunk the cup of inner meanings from the hand of utterance in this Paradise which God hath sanctified from allusions and limitations.

order.why: Read joy, illumination, and the spring of life as images of meeting.
Read favor and the long-concealed wine as images of encounter.
shortened: Blessed is he who has found himself in My presence, attained to My favor, and drunk from the choice wine of My bounty which has been sealed from time immemorial and concealed from the eyes of My servants and My creation.

order.why: Join presence with good pleasure and contentment.
Keep gratitude for the meeting and the ocean of attainment.
Read the face, horizon, and sealed wine images together.
Consider the blessing on an eye that sees and receives the Pen’s traces.
Read utterance and acknowledgment as aspects of participation.
Keep the brief joy of witnessing and meeting.
shortened: Joy to those who have attained to witnessing and meeting, and woe to the deniers."

order.why: Consider the source’s testimony concerning those who attain the light.
shortened: Verily he who hath attained unto the lights of the Countenance is among those who have attained the presence of God upon His throne - to this do honored servants bear witness.

order.why: Explains attaining the divine Presence through the Manifestations.
Preserve the blessing’s source omission without inventing its missing continuation.
shortened: Happy is the eye that seeth, and the face that turneth towards, the Countenance of God, the Lord of all being....

order.why: Read the testimony to the desire to stand and listen.
Consider the illumination of those who turn toward the countenance.
shortened: Through Him have shone forth the faces of those who have turned towards My luminous Countenance which gleams above all who are in earth and heaven.

order.why: Keep the source’s valuation of these souls in its selected setting.
Read joy in drawing near, hearing, and knowing.
shortened: O what joy for those who draw nigh unto them and hear their melody and attain to their knowledge! And peace be upon you.

order.why: Turn from testimony toward acting on what has been received.
shortened: This, verily, is a noble station. Bear thou witness unto that whereunto God hath testified, then act according to that which thou hast been bidden by One Who is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

order.why: Read the commission to return and share what was seen and known.
shortened: O Ismi al-Asdaq! Render thanks for that We called thee to appear before the Divine Presence, caused thee to hear and to behold the effulgences of the countenance of thy Lord, the Most Exalted, the Incomparable, the One, the Great; and sent thee back that thou mightest remind the people of that which thou didst behold and know, and summon them unto the Most Great Steadfastness, lest their feet slip by reason of the clamour of every sinful pretender.

order.why: Consider gratitude, hearing, response, and steadfastness over time.
Keep the personal invitation to give thanks for the meeting.
shortened: O faithful, supplicating, pure, good, steadfast, and successful leaf! Praise the Ancient Beauty and the Most Great Name that in the days of God you attained the presence of the Beloved of the horizons and the Purpose of the essence of existence among the people of concord.

order.why: Read the repeated call to grateful remembrance.
Consider listening and the cup of union in the source’s devotional language.
shortened: You heard the words and hearkened to the divine address and became intoxicated from the overflowing cup brimming with the wine of meeting, dripping with the sweetness of union.

order.why: Read years of hearing beside firmness in the Covenant.
shortened: Thou who art the fruit of that tree and the memorial of that aged elder - praise be to God that for many years thou wert honored to attain the presence of the Beauty of the Lord and wert blessed to hearken unto the Word of grace and wert accepted at the Divine Threshold and art firm in God's Covenant and Testament.

order.why: Keep the gratitude for existence in the cycle and shelter under the tree.
shortened: Thank God that in such a cycle ye have stepped into the plane of existence, attained the glory of the Lord of the Kingdom, obtained light from the Sun of Truth and were ushered in under the shadow of the Tree of Life in the paradise of joy.

order.why: Read the recipient’s father’s visit and the favors ascribed to it.
Consider the daughter’s remembrance of her father’s service and encounter.
Keep the remembrance of a mother who attained presence.
Read bereavement alongside a remembered life of faith and encounter.
Consider the source’s assurance concerning one who has died.
shortened: Say: Verily he who has died from among you has been raised unto God and God is witness to this. By God! He has returned to the Primal Point in a mighty and impregnable station.

order.why: Read fish, sea, lover, and reunion as images of fulfillment.
shortened: That thirsty fish has found its way to the sea of reunion, and that sugar-breaking parrot has attained to honey and repeated sweetness. That burning-hearted lover has attained to the radiant-faced Beloved, and that noble friend has received the portion of meeting the heart-attracting Loved One.

order.why: Consider nearness in the eternal world when outward meeting was not achieved.
shortened: Though attainment to the divine presence may not be possible in this transient world, in the eternal world the spiritual state of success and prosperity is assured.

order.why: Read the promise of spiritual attainment beyond earthly disappointment.
Keep the expectation of meeting in the most exalted horizon.
Consider presence in a realm beyond present comprehension.
Read the hope of release from separation into witnessing and meeting.
Consider remembered presence in the hearts of the Beloved’s lovers.
Keep the reported presence of heart and spirit across bodily distance.
shortened: When the believers gather in a meeting and are engaged in the mention of God my heart is there, my spirit is there, although my body may be a thousand miles away...

order.why: Read the reported affirmation of Christ’s enduring presence.
Keep the account of a dream clearly attributed to its reported experience.
Read the reported gratitude for pilgrimage and shared amity.
shortened: You must be very thankful to God for He brought you to this Holy Land to visit the Blessed Tomb, and to sit down with Me in absolute love and amity.

order.why: Consider the reported orientation of thought and face during prayer.
shortened: "When I pray I turn My thoughts and My face to the Blessed Perfection."

order.why: Keep the source’s instruction concerning the point of adoration.
Read the appeal to seek assistance from the unseen world.
Consider the invitation to seek presence and carry glad tidings.
shortened: Now become thou a seeker of His presence, that thou mayest witness Him in the Kingdom of the Unseen and give glad tidings and good news to the world.

order.why: Read the personal assurance of acceptance and grace.
Hear the repeated call into the Kingdom and paradise.
Read the prayer for shelter, guidance, and the ocean of love.
shortened: Perchance I may find shelter at Thy Divine Threshold, go to the adored Sanctuary of Thy Divine Essence, walk in the way of Thy guidance and swim in the ocean of Thy Love.

order.why: Consider the prayer to stand at the universally opened door of mercy.
shortened: I beseech Thee to ordain for me presence before Thy throne and to enable me to stand at the door of Thy mercy, which hath been opened unto all who are in Thy heaven and on Thy earth.

order.why: Read the sole desire for presence and the garden of beauty.
shortened: Their sole desire was to attain unto Thy presence, to enter the garden of Thy beauty, to arrive at the sanctuary of reunion with Thee, to prostrate themselves before the gate of Thy mercy, and to bow down before Thy countenance.

order.why: Keep the brief petition for presence and visitation.
Read the prayer for another person’s meeting and beauty.
Consider the prayer to open the gates before seekers.
Read the request to be numbered among those who turn and attain.
shortened: Then make me to be among those who turned unto Thee until they attained unto presence before Thy throne and were blessed with the Kawthar of Thy meeting and the Tasnim of reunion with Thee.

order.why: Consider the prayer for those who follow the path of love.
shortened: I call upon Thee by Thy Name through which Thou didst raise up the heavens upon the thread of Thine eternity and didst elevate the pavilions of the Cause upon the throne of the glory of Thine oneness, that Thou mayest send down upon those who have mentioned Thy Most Exalted Name and who have followed the path of Thy love in the realm below, and then raise them up, O my God, unto the stations of holiness in Thy presence, that they may dwell in Thy habitations and drink from the cup of Thy good-pleasure.

order.why: Read the plea for ascent to the station of witnessing.
Keep the prayer for an enduring abode in mercy and meeting.
shortened: O my Lord! Suffer him to abide in a blessed abode and cause him to enter into a retreat of faithfulness and favor him to everlastingly dwell in the heavenly paradise, the precinct of meeting in the shelter of Thy great mercy!

order.why: Close with the prayer for nearness and the wine of wondrous utterance.
shortened: We beseech God that He may draw thee nigh unto Him and cause thee to enter the holy presence and give thee to drink of the choice wine of His wondrous and glorious utterance.

questions: How do these readings relate the unknowability of the divine Essence to the possibility of meeting and knowing through the Manifestation?
What roles do justice, belief, listening, and inward turning play in the meaning of presence?
How do invitations to visit and assurances to those prevented from visiting illuminate different forms of nearness?
What new possibilities for remembrance or service appear in the accounts of separation and bereavement?
How does Philip’s question in John help you examine the relationship between seeing, knowing, words, and works, while attending to each tradition’s language?
Which connected subject on mediation, recognition, or prayer would deepen your understanding of the encounter described here?
